articles.title: Why has Shafali Verma been reprimanded by the ICC after India's win over Zimbabwe?
articles.summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the
articles.body: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe.The incident took place during India's nine-wicket win in Raipur on Sunday. The 22-year-old was found guilty of breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct.What happened during the match?The incident took place in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings. Shafali dropped a catch offered by Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling. She then threw the ball to the ground in frustration.The ICC found that Shafali had breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel. This rule deals with the “abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match,” an ICC media release said.One demerit point added to her recordAlong with the official reprimand, one demerit point has been added to Shafali's disciplinary record. This was her first offence in a 24-month period.Shafali admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by G.S. Lakshmi of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees. As a result, there was no need for a formal hearing.On-field umpires Vrinda Rathi and Gayathri Venugopalan, third umpire Anna Harris and fourth umpire Janani Narayanan levelled the charge.What is the penalty for a Level 1 breach?Level 1 breaches of the ICC Code of Conduct carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand. The maximum punishment is a fine of 50 per cent of a player's match fee, along with one or two demerit points.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ICC T20I Rankings: Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma dominate as Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud make gains
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s dominance in the ICC Women’s T20I Bowling Rankings continues, with Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma retaining the top two positions,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s dominance in the ICC Women’s T20I Bowling Rankings continues, with Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma retaining the top two positions, while fast bowlers Nandani Sharma and Kranti Gaud made significant gains following the ongoing series against Zimbabwe.India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series at home, with their bowlers playing a key role in the campaign. The latest rankings reflect the depth of India’s bowling resources, with Nandani and Kranti rewarded for their performances in the first two matches in Raipur.Nandani emerged as one of the biggest movers, climbing 26 places to 45th in the T20I bowling rankings. The right-arm seamer has claimed three wickets across the first two matches, making her one of the joint-leading wicket-takers in the series.Teammate Kranti also made progress, moving up nine places to 43rd. Their rise adds to the achievements of Charani and Deepti, who remain first and second, respectively, after delivering economical performances against Zimbabwe.Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma maintain their gripCharani continues to lead the T20I bowling rankings, with experienced all-rounder Deepti occupying second place. Their continued presence at the summit underlines India’s strength in the shortest format, where spin has remained a key component of the bowling attack.The latest update also highlights the growing contribution of India’s pace options. Nandani’s 26-place jump and Kranti’s rise of nine positions show how the performances of the supporting bowlers are strengthening the team’s resources ahead of future international assignments.New Zealand bowlers and batters make gainsThere were also changes in the T20I rankings following the opening match of the trans-Tasman series between Australia and New Zealand in Sydney.Australia seamer Annabel Sutherland climbed one place to eighth among T20I bowlers, while New Zealand’s Jess Kerr rose five spots to 17th. Teammates Bree Illing and Nensi Patel also improved, moving up six places to 23rd and five places to 35th, respectively.New Zealand batters Maddy Green and Georgia Plimmer made progress in the T20I batting rankings. Green climbed three places to 34th, while Plimmer made a significant 13-place jump to 48th.Australia’s Beth Mooney, meanwhile, retained her position as the world’s top-ranked T20I batter.Megan Schutt, Ellyse Perry rise in ODI rankingsThe latest update also brought gains for Australian players in the ODI rankings following their 50-over series against Bangladesh in the ICC Women’s Championship.Veteran fast bowler Megan Schutt moved up one place to fourth in the ODI bowling rankings. Ellyse Perry climbed one spot to ninth among ODI batters and made an even bigger jump in the all-rounders’ list, rising 14 places to 25th.Sutherland also benefited from her unbeaten half-century in the final ODI, moving up four places to 13th in the batting rankings. Bangladesh batter Sharmin Akhter Supta climbed five places to 25th.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Hundred 2027 will allow teams to field four overseas players in playing XI in increase from previous seasons
articles.summary: Faf du Plessis, Shadab Khan and Daryl Mitchell among those to miss out in 2026 auction, who could stand a greater chance of being signed next year as the number of overseas players allowed in a squad increases from four to five, and in playing XIs from three to four
articles.body:
Before the direct signing window from January 20 - February 3, and the auction - set for March but the date yet to confirmed - teams can first look to secure their favourite players from 2026.

Also, in a change to squad sizes for 2027, teams can now carry a maximum of 19 players (and minimum of 16), with the number of overseas players allowed rising from four to five - and from three to four in playing XIs.

Here's everything you need to know about The Hundred retention window and more:

When does the retention window open and close?

The window opened on October 19, 2026 and closes on January 15, 2027. Teams can announce retained players from their 2026 squads at any point during this period.

Each men's and women's squad can retain up to 16 players. Retained players will stay on their 2026 salaries for the 2027 season.

Teams can retain any player signed at The Hundred Auction 2026, including those who subsequently didn't play in the 2026 competition due to injury or unavailability.

They can also retain any replacement player who played at least two games in the 2026 competition.

Players selected in the Vitality Wildcard Draft in 2026 can be retained at their base price or on an increased salary for 2027, but they will not count as wildcards next season if retained.

What happens to players who aren't retained?

Unretained players remain eligible to be signed during the direct signing window, either by their existing team or by another team. They may also choose to enter the auction in March.

The direct signing window runs from January 20 to February 3. During this period, teams can sign eligible players directly before finalising their squads at auction.

As in 2026, teams can make up to four direct signings if they have space in their squad. This includes a maximum of two domestic players and a maximum of two overseas players.

Overseas player and squad size updates for 2027

The maximum number of overseas players in a squad has increased from four to five, with four allowed in the playing XI - up from three. This additional overseas player is only available, should teams opt for it.

Squad sizes have increased to a maximum of 19 players for 2027.

The Hundred Auction will take place in early March 2027. The exact date will be announced in due course.

articles.title: IND W vs ZIM W: India women thrash Zimbabwe by 92 runs to seal 3-0 T20I series sweep
articles.body: The post-match Presentation.... Coach's word - Following a successful series, India Head Coach Amol Muzumdar expresses immense satisfaction with the team's performance and execution on the field as they prepare to head to Baroda (Vadodara). He highlights the impactful contributions of youngsters like Niki Prasad, who shows her class in the opening game, and Anushka, alongside a crucial innings from Harmanpreet Kaur. Emphasising the team's overarching philosophy, Muzumdar notes that the squad successfully translates their dressing room discussions into action, maintaining a ruthless and dominant brand of cricket throughout their recent T20 matches.. Shafali's fireworks, Harmanpreet's vintage show - India walked out with a fresh opening combination, Anushka Sharma joining Shafali Verma at the top, but the intent stayed unchanged. Shafali smashed a swashbuckling 50 to keep the scoreboard racing, while Anushka, promoted up the order, played a brisk hand of her own. Then came Harmanpreet, who began quietly before flipping the switch and hammering an unbeaten 91, clearing the ropes with ease and finding gaps at will. Zimbabwe's catching held up well, apart from a couple of spills, but their bowlers had no answer to India's batting onslaught.. Nandani, the wrecker in chief - India had enough runs on the board against a very inexperienced side, but they still needed to pick up wickets. Niki Prasad and Kranti Gaud struck early, though India went through a lean patch in the middle overs without adding to the tally. The return of Nandani Sharma, however, broke the back of the Zimbabwean innings, and she finished with three wickets. Arundhati, a touch more expensive than she would have liked, also chipped in with a wicket, as did Deepti, who was her usual economical self with a scalp to her name.. Improvements made, but not enough - Zimbabwe showed a slight uptick in their approach tonight. Yes, they lost two early wickets, but Biza and Mayers kept the scoreboard ticking with regular strike rotation. The boundary percentage was not great again, but the real positive was that they avoided losing wickets in clusters this time around. Eventually, it was Mayers who tried to shift gears and brought up a well-compiled fifty, surviving a couple of dropped chances along the way. But Niki Prasad broke the 82-run stand to keep India firmly on the front foot. Beloved Biza also played a fine knock of 44, but barring the two, none of the batter could cross double figures, which is still a worrying pattern for the tourists.. Too hot to handle - The Women in Blue once again came out on top in Raipur, outplaying the Lady Chevrons in every department. It was another one-sided contest, but Zimbabwe did show a bit more fight compared to their previous two outings. This is India's biggest T20I win by run margin at home, and it also extends their winning streak to 11 matches in the format, including the Asia Cup in the UAE and the Asian Games in Japan. articles.title: 'Where are the fans?': David Warner fumes over sparse crowds in South Africa-Australia Test series
articles.summary: The ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia has sparked a debate over the popularity of red-ball cricket, with former Australian opener
articles.body: The ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia has sparked a debate over the popularity of red-ball cricket, with former Australian opener David Warner expressing disappointment over the lack of spectators at the venues. Despite featuring the world's top two Test teams, the series has struggled to draw sizeable crowds, prompting Warner to question whether the format is thriving.The stands were largely empty during the opening Test at Kingsmead in Durban, while rain further affected attendance during the first two days of the second Test at St George's Park in Gqeberha. The sparse crowds have raised concerns, particularly given the stature of the contest and its significance for both sides.David Warner questions Test cricket's popularity"We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving?" Warner wrote on X."You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic," he added.South Africa-Australia series struggles to draw crowdsThe series carries considerable significance, with Australia entering as the world's top-ranked Test side and South Africa placed second. It is also Australia's first Test tour of South Africa since the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, while the Proteas are playing their first home Test series as reigning world Test champions.Despite the high-profile nature of the contest, the turnout has been underwhelming. The opening Test, which South Africa lost by 214 runs, attracted just under 20,000 spectators across five days at Kingsmead, less than a fifth of the venue's capacity.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Ajay Kookna's twin strikes keep Rajasthan in control against Railways
articles.summary: JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Kookna’s timely twin strikes broke two crucial partnerships to derail a solid Railways recovery, keeping Rajasthan firmly in
articles.body: JAIPUR: Left-arm spinner Ajay Kookna’s timely twin strikes broke two crucial partnerships to derail a solid Railways recovery, keeping Rajasthan firmly in the driver’s seat on Day Three at the Sawai Man Singh Stadium. Railways finished the day at 305/6, still trailing by 192 runs behind the hosts' massive first-innings total, despite a gritty 73-run (203 balls) resistance from captain Bhargav Merai.After starting the day from 46/1, Railways lost two quick wickets in the opening session to pacers Danish Bhambhu and Akash Singh before mounting a recovery. Merai first partnered with Eshaan Goyal (64 off 164) to put together 98 runs.Kookna provided the much-needed first breakthrough after lunch by trapping Goyal lbw, ending their threatening stand. Following this, Merai found another fluent ally in Ravi Singh (53 off 75).Explaining the tactical shift after the break, Kookna pointed out that while they initially expected the pitch to offer help, it did not, so the target was simply to restrict runs by hitting consistent areas. “As the ball gets older, it stops turning, so the new ball helped us break the partnership," he said after the day’s play.The Railways’ pair frustrated the hosts with an 83-run alliance, before Kookna halted their momentum in the final session with his second decisive strike of the day, having the Railways skipper stumped.Soon after, pacer Chetan Sharma removed Ravi, who was caught behind, to reduce the visitors to 256/6.The Railways skipper conceded that when that partnership broke, the momentum shifted. “Our partnership was very crucial. If I had stayed at the crease, we would surely have had the upper hand,” he said.Refusing to surrender, Zubair Ali (18 not out off 33 balls) and Toufik Mondal (33 not out off 48 balls) stitched together an unbroken lower-order resistance through the rest of the evening. The pair narrowed the deficit, keeping alive hopes of avoiding the follow-on as the match heads into the final day.Merai said that they were originally looking to chase the 497-run total. “I have seen big totals being chased down here, so that was our goal. If we had scored 300 for 4, we could still be in the game, but we lost two extra wickets. Zubair scored 100 last year and won two Player-of-the-Match awards, so we are still hopeful of a good partnership of 100 runs, and then things can change," he said."The pitch has gone slower. There is some patch at the far end, so Kookna will be crucial for them on the last day. If we can deal with him, great,” the Railways captain added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan vs England: Sloppy visitors floored by Arafat Minhas in Rawalpindi
articles.summary: England begin their wandering winter with a sloppy loss to Pakistan in the one-day tri-series in Rawalpindi.
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi

Pakistan 302-9 (50 overs): Baker 3-65; Nawaz 79 (74), Arafat 59 (58)

England 215 (38.4 overs): Banton 57 (53), Arafat 6-40

England began their wandering winter with a sloppy loss to Pakistan in the one-day tri-series in Rawalpindi.

In the opening match of five separate tours to four different countries on three continents, England's mistakes opened the door for Pakistan's Arafat Minhas to take advantage.

The all-rounder made a crucial 59 with the bat, then bamboozled England by taking 6-40 with his left-arm spin.

Asked to bat, Pakistan were 190-5 in the 37th over when diving wicketkeeper Jordan Cox put down Arafat on 12, one of three catches England dropped.

Arafat, alongside a powerful 79 from Hasan Nawaz, lifted Pakistan to 302-9.

Faced with making the second-highest score to win an ODI at the Rawalpindi Stadium, England made a rapid start to the chase, only for further errors to let Pakistan back in.

At 91-0, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull to depart for 45 and, crucially, Tom Banton was caught for 57 when he shovelled Arafat's long hop to mid-wicket.

Arafat's fine all-round performance continued with a beautiful delivery to bowl England captain Harry Brook for five and Naseem Shah got one to keep low to bowl Joe Root for 33.

When Cox was lbw and Jamie Overton holed out, both off Arafat, England were floored. They spluttered to 215 all out, losing their last seven wickets for 50 runs, capped by a calamitous run out of Gus Atkinson.

Pakistan have two wins from two in the tri-series and are already on the brink of the final, while England next meet Sri Lanka at the same ground on Thursday, with both sides looking for their first victory.

Winter and World Cup countdown start with defeat

Not only is this the beginning of England's winter – two trips to Australia and Test tours of South Africa and Bangladesh follow – but also the start of a long run-in to the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa next year.

This was the first of a potential 21 ODIs in preparation for the World Cup, the tri-series format designed to replicate the pressure and permutations of tournament cricket.

In fairness to England, they have improved in ODI cricket - winning their three previous series this year - and they were without three first-choice players in Jos Buttler, Jofra Archer and Jacob Bethell.

Nevertheless, this was a game they could have won had they not wasted their opportunities, while squad players missed chances to press their case. Cox dropped two catches behind the stumps, Sonny Baker was expensive with the new ball and Banton squandered the platform to make a huge score at the top of the order.

The outcome was a defeat in their first ODI in Pakistan since 2005 and a loss in their first taste of tri-series ODI cricket since 2015.

To focus on England's shortcomings would be a disservice to Pakistan, who are a vastly different proposition in this format on home soil to the team soundly beaten in the Test series in the UK last month.

From 133-5 in the 28th over, the hosts could have wilted, yet Nawaz's slog-sweep for six from the first ball he faced from Adil Rashid was the beginning of Pakistan's fightback.

Along with Arafat and Faheem Ashraf, Nawaz carried Pakistan to what seemed no more than a competitive total on a flat pitch.

When night fell, Arafat produced his magical spell to the delight of a noisy full house.

He produced the best figures by a Pakistan spinner in an ODI against England, then Arafat also ran out Atkinson to complete the hosts' win.

Bavuma epic drags SA back into Test - have they time to beat Australia?

England coach should be English, suggests Fleming

How one rule change is altering the face of one-day cricket

This was a good test for England's batting, not unlike the kind of chase they can expect to face at the World Cup, albeit in different conditions.

Much like when they were tasked with overhauling 325 to beat Sri Lanka at Headingley in an ODI less than a month ago, they fell short.

Banton made a century in that series but knows the injured Bethell will be back for the tour of Australia next month. Another hundred would have made the selection decision difficult, explaining Banton's obvious disappointment when he somehow belted Arafat to Shaheen Afridi.

Cox will have a run in the ODI side because Buttler is out until at least the new year and the Essex man will also have an eye on securing a place in the Test team in South Africa.

At number six, Cox had the opportunity to make amends for his two drops, yet he was deceived by the wily Arafat to be lbw for 18.

In between, England lost their biggest wickets. Brook was all at sea in missing a beautiful turning delivery from Arafat, Root was arguably unlucky to be bowled by Naseem and Sam Curran, playing for the first time since The Hundred, shovelled to deep square leg.

When Curran departed for 27, England were 177-5 midway through the 32nd over and the game was beginning to slip away.

What followed was Arafat singled-handedly ripping through the lower order.

Cox was done in the flight to be leg before, Overton was caught at long-on and Will Jacks, so often England's saviour in white-ball cricket, found the hands of mid-wicket.

Rashid was palpably leg before and the mix-up between Baker and Atkinson that resulted in the latter face down on the turf epitomised England's collapse.

It was another chapter in England's long history of capitulating to spin on the sub-continent.

England captain Harry Brook: "We were quite happy with 300. We thought they were slightly under par. It got dewy as we thought it would do. We were pretty happy at halfway."

On not pushing on after a strong opening partnership: "That was the story of the innings. We thought [Tom] Banton, Ducky [Ben Duckett] set the tone to get a 100 partnership and then it was a case of losing too many wickets in clumps, we couldn't string the partnerships together and we ended up on the wrong side."

On where they will look to do better next time: "You always want to win, don't you? We've spoken a lot about rotation of strike through the middle but I think we were a little too careful against the spinners especially, so we can probably put them under a little bit more pressure in stages and we've got to tonight to talk about it and tomorrow and bounce back better on Thursday."

articles.title: Temba Bavuma hits Test-best 179 as South Africa dominate Australia on day three of second Test in Gqeberha
articles.summary: Kagiso Rabada takes wicket with fourth ball on Test return as South Africa reduce Australia to 3-1 by stumps in Gqeberha, trailing by 422 after Temba Bavuma's earlier 179; watch day four of second Test, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8.30am, Wednesday (play starts 9am)
articles.body:
Bavuma's magnificent innings helped rescue the Proteas from a perilous position of 40-4, with Australia's bowlers on top during the first two rain-affected days in Gqeberha but Bavuma, along with vital lower-order contributions from Marco Jansen (85) and Simon Harmer (82) helped wrestle the match the home side's way.

Kagiso Rabada only added to their advantage by striking with his fourth ball back from a hamstring injury that has sidelined him since June, with Nic Maddinson poking an edge to third slip for his second duck in three innings since his own Test return.

Australia ultimately closed on 3-1, still trailing South Africa by 422 runs on first innings, though with so much time lost to wet weather already in the Test match, the hosts are up against the clock over the final two days in their push for victory and force a series-decider in Cape Town from October 27.

South Africa resumed the third morning on 97-5 and swiftly lost a sixth wicket as Wiaan Mulder (13) was bounced out by Mitchell Starc for his 450th Test wicket.

But Bavuma continued to battle, notching a 140-ball fifty, before he and Jansen provided the perfect counter-punch in a 132-run partnership for the seventh wicket, one which was only bettered by the 183 put with Harmer - a new South African record stand for the eighth wicket.

Scott Boland (5-81), who had torn through the Proteas' top order over the first two days, secured a well-deserved five-for with the dismissal of Jansen, while Harmer and Bavuma's resistance was finally broken with back-to-back deliveries to trigger a declaration on 425-9.

Marnus Labuschagne first bowled Harmer, before Starc was the one to finally draw an error from Bavuma as he nicked off for 179.

Rabada added to Australia's woes with his early dismissal of Maddison, though he was restricted to just the one over as the deteriorating light resulted in three subsequent overs of spin prior to stumps.

Former Australia batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series in South Africa.

South Africa lost the first Test match by 214 runs in Durban , with large sections of the Kingsmead ground empty, and the crowds haven't really picked up through the first two rain-affected days of the second Test in Gqeberha.

"We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa?" Warner said in a social media post on Tuesday.

"Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we're supposed to believe the format is thriving?

"You can't keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it.

"Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic."

Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was part of the infamous 'sandpapergate' scandal that dominated Australia's last tour of South Africa in 2018. The then vice-captain was given a one-year ban and told he would never be considered for a leadership position within the team again.

articles.title: England slump to defeat against Pakistan in ODI tri-series after faltering chasing 303 in Rawalpindi
articles.summary: England lose last seven wickets for just 50 runs, bowled out for 215 in 38.4 overs chasing 303 to win; wheels come off after opening stand of 91 between Ben Duckett (45) and Tom Banton (57) snapped; Pakistan's Arafat Minhas takes 6-40 and secures winning run out after maiden ODI fifty
articles.body:
England, who have won their last three bilateral ODI series, were cruising on 91-0 inside 15 overs in a chase of 303, only to end up being bowled out for 215 in 38.4, losing their final seven wickets for just 50 runs, as home spinner Arafat Minhas backed up his maiden ODI half-century with figures of 6-40 in a stunning performance.

Visiting captain Harry Brook (5) was bowled by a beauty from Arafat after Ben Duckett (45) and Tom Banton (57) failed to build on a rollicking opening stand against a Pakistan side who had rallied from 81-4 to 302-9 earlier in the day having being put in to bat.

The tourists wilted once the hosts snapped a partnership of 31 from 57 balls between Joe Root (33) and Sam Curran (27) from 128-3, with Arafat on a hat-trick after removing Will Jacks (19) and Adil Rashid (1) from successive deliveries in the 39th over before he ran out Gus Atkinson (7) two balls later to clinch victory.

Arafat was involved in each of the final five wickets, including those of Jamie Overton (1), who holed out at long-on in what commentator Stuart Broad described as "an appalling dismissal", and Jordan Cox (18), who fell lbw.

England are back in action against Sri Lanka at the same venue on Thursday ( 9am UK, live on Sky Sports ) in a tournament which sees the three sides play each other twice before the top two in the table meet in a final in Lahore on October 31.

England strike from first ball of the match

Brook's men - whose feast of white-ball cricket continues in Australia in November with three ODIs and five T20s - were on top at various points on Tuesday, starting from the very first ball when Atkinson (2-35) had Fakhar Zaman (0) caught at midwicket.

Fakhar, pouched low by Root, was one of four batters to fall inside 19 overs, with opening partner Saim Ayub (8) bounced out by seamer Sonny Baker (3-65) after being starved of the strike and Babar Azam (34) bowled playing back to off-spinner Jacks.

When leg-spinner Rashid, back from a hand injury that saw him miss the 2-1 win at home to Sri Lanka in September, had Salman Ali Agha - a centurion against Sri Lanka on Sunday - caught sweeping a full toss, you wondered if Pakistan would bat out the overs.

But Shaheen Shah Afridi's side managed that thanks to a middle and lower-order counterattack led by Hasan Nawaz (79 off 74), who pumped his first ball, bowled by Rashid, for six amid nine boundaries all told during his second ODI fifty.

The 24-year-old shared fifty stands with Arafat (59) and Saad Baig (35), while there was then an alliance of 72 from just 49 deliveries between Arafat and Faheem Ashraf (39 off 26).

England sloppy in the field before fluffing lines with the bat

England, who conceded 80 runs from the final eight overs, dropped three catches - Atkinson with one of them and Cox, deputising as wicketkeeper for the injured Jos Buttler (hamstring), guilty of two - while Curran (1-40 off five overs) looked rusty with the ball having not played since The Hundred in August owing to a groin problem.

Pakistan's total was looking ever so lean as Banton and Duckett fired early on - Banton notching his third successive fifty-plus score and third in four knocks since replacing Jacob Bethell (knee) at the top of the order.

However, when Duckett was bounced out by Haris Rauf (2-32) and Arafat had Banton cloth to midwicket and castled Brook with a peach that straightened after gripping, the wobble was on.

Root and Curran stemmed Pakistan's fightback initially, only for Root to be poleaxed by a Naseem Shah ball that kept low and Curran to heave Rauf to deep backward square.

articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Temba Bavuma century drags hosts back into series
articles.summary: Captain Temba Bavuma drags South Africa back into their Test series against Australia but did his side bat on too long on day three?
articles.body:
Second Test, Gqeberha (day three of five)

South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81

Captain Temba Bavuma dragged South Africa back into their Test series against Australia with a masterful 179 on day three in Gqeberha.

Bavuma, who emerged in the gloom at 12-2 on day one, batted for 552 minutes across three days in making his highest Test score, allowing the Proteas to declare on 425-9 with half an hour to play having been 110-6 earlier on day three.

Kagiso Rabada nicked off Australia opener Nic Maddinson in the first over of Australia's reply to further boost the hosts' cause.

Bavuma's knock was every bit as impressive as Matthew Renshaw's 190 for Australia in their first Test win - arguably more so given the momentum that had built behind Australia since South Africa's batting struggles and the quality of the tourists' attack.

He remained composed in sharing partnerships of 132 with Marco Jansen and 183 with number nine Simon Harmer - the best eighth-wicket partnership in South Africa's Test history.

The century was Bavuma's fifth in Tests - 10 years after his first made him the first Black African to score a Test hundred for the Proteas.

He said it was "definitely" one of his best innings.

"That bowling attack, at least three are in the top 10 of the bowling rankings," he added. "There is a reason why."

More relevant for this series and England's tour to come over Christmas, it was Bavuma's fourth century in 14 Tests as South Africa captain.

He now averages 54.36 as Test skipper, compared with 34.53 across 93 innings before taking the reins. Few can match that improvement.

Should South Africa have declared earlier?

It was Bavuma's dismissal - caught behind off Mitchell Starc - which triggered South Africa's decision to declare with half an hour to go in the day.

They had resisted doing so earlier in the session and when Harmer was bowled by Marnus Labuschagne a ball before the Bavuma wicket.

With the floodlights on and skies dark, conditions were perfect for seam bowling when Australia's reply began. Maddinson was only able to resist four deliveries before nicking to third slip.

The umpires then deemed the light too poor for seam bowling to continue, however, and after three overs of spin with the new ball the players left the field.

Had South Africa declared earlier, Jansen could have bowled in tandem with Rabada in the gloom.

"There was thought of that," Bavuma said. "I was a little hesitant because of the weather.

"If we [had declared] a bit early we would have got one or two more overs. Saying that we got the one we wanted.

"Right now I hope things go our way and we set ourselves to be on the field for the majority of those two days."

After only 42 overs were possible across the first two days, South Africa now have an outside shot at victory over days four and five, ideally by dismissing Australia cheaply and enforcing the follow-on.

"We have given ourselves a chance," Bavuma said.

"There is the other side of the draw but going into [the third Test in] Cape Town whatever the confidence we can get here, being able to put their bowlers on their feet for a considerable amount of time, hopefully that can pay off in the long run."
